extra.message: The unauthenticated /cwe95/rgbToHex endpoint passes the red, green, and blue query parameters directly to eval(). Each parameter permits arbitrary server-side JavaScript execution with the Node.js process's privileges. The additional argument 10 does not restrict eval().

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: Query parameters can evaluate to strings containing HTML. converter.rgbToHex() preserves those strings through toString(16) and concatenation, and res.send(hex) returns them without escaping. Supplying red as the JavaScript string literal '<script>alert(1)</script>' and green=0&blue=0 produces reflected XSS. String responses default to HTML in the [Express implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expressjs/express/4.17.1/lib/response.js).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The unauthenticated /cwe73/read endpoint passes req.query.foo directly to fse.readJsonSync() and returns the parsed contents. Relative traversal sequences and absolute paths are accepted without directory restrictions, allowing disclosure of any readable valid JSON file, including configuration or credential files outside the application directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: An unauthenticated caller controls the path read synchronously by fse.readJsonSync(), without file-type or size checks. On Linux, foo=/dev/zero selects a device that never reaches EOF, causing continuous reading and memory consumption while blocking the server's event loop. JSON validation occurs only after reading, so it cannot prevent this denial of service.

The /cwe79/echo endpoint concatenates req.query.text directly into an HTML paragraph without escaping. A text value containing <script>alert(1)</script> executes in the application's origin when a victim opens the crafted URL. The [Express implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expressjs/express/4.17.1/lib/response.js) sends this string as HTML.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /cwe113/split endpoint lets callers choose both a response header name and its value through res.append(req.query.key, req.query.value). Using key=Refresh&value=0%3Burl%3Dhttps%3A%2F%2Fattacker.example causes browser navigation to an attacker-controlled site without destination validation. This uses a valid header and requires no CRLF injection; Refresh navigation is defined by the [HTML Standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#shared-declarative-refresh-steps).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The /cwe201/exposure endpoint sends req.query.text directly as the response body. A string such as <script>alert(1)</script> is returned unescaped and executes in the application's origin when a victim visits the crafted URL. The [Express implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expressjs/express/4.17.1/lib/response.js) defaults string responses to text/html.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The unauthenticated /cwe502/serialize endpoint passes req.query.foo directly to serialize.unserialize(). The [deserializer implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luin/serialize/master/lib/serialize.js) evaluates strings prefixed with _$$ND_FUNC$$_; an immediately invoked function in attacker-supplied JSON therefore executes arbitrary server-side JavaScript during deserialization. test/server.js:133 also contains an example payload.

The unauthenticated /cwe78/childprocess endpoint passes req.query.foo directly to child_process.exec(). Callers control the entire shell command, allowing arbitrary operating-system commands to execute with the server process's privileges. Returning a fixed response does not prevent execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The script embeds literal VERACODE_API_KEY_ID and VERACODE_API_KEY_SECRET values and passes them into the agent-server container on line 5. Anyone with repository access obtains the authentication material and can use it if the credentials remain active. Credential validity was not tested.

The pipeline executes curl --silent --insecure ${AGENT_SERVER_URL}/downloads | sh. Disabling TLS certificate verification allows an attacker who intercepts the agent-server connection to impersonate the server and replace the downloaded script, which is immediately executed with the build runner's privileges.

The test script downloads executable content using curl --insecure -sSL ${AGENT_SERVER_URL}/downloads | sh. Certificate verification is disabled before the response is executed. With the configured localhost endpoint, an attacker able to impersonate the local agent service on port 10010 can supply a script that runs with the invoking user's privileges.
